claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Qualification, IV-18' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Restriction, VI-1'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Qualification, IV-18' then '  Restriction, VI-1'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page B-60 (PDF p972) and page-972.md carry the same entries in the same order, one per line, with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry (e.g. 'Qualification, IV-18' / '  Restriction, VI-1'; 'Punctuation characters, III-18' / 'Format punctuation, IV-2' / 'Separators, IV-4'; 'Record description entry, III-19, IV-33,' with continuation 'IV-34'). The claim itself concedes the entry text and page references match. The only difference is Markdown rendering style (bare indented lines vs. '- ' list markers used on other pages), which is formatting of an informative index and changes no content or meaning.
